title: Morpho-kinematics of the circumstellar envelope of the AGB star R Dor: a global view
question: Characterise the global morpho-kinematics (rotation, expansion, turbulence, absorption, south-eastern blue-shifted stream, and broad outflows) of the circumstellar envelope of the oxygen-rich AGB star R Dor from the stellar surface up to ~100 au.

data.arrays: 12m array (44-45 antennas for 2017.1.00191.S; average 35 antennas for 2013.1.00166.S; average 45 antennas for 2017.1.00824.S)
data.angular_resolution: ~2.3 au (34x25 mas^2 in CASA, 41x35 mas^2 in GILDAS for 29SiO/SO2); 220x170 mas^2 (28SiO II), 180x140 mas^2 (CO), 157x145 mas^2 (HCN), 154x147 mas^2 / 9 au (SO)
data.sensitivity: 1.4 mJy beam^-1 (29SiO), 1.1 mJy beam^-1 (SO2), 18 mJy beam^-1 (28SiO II), 14 mJy beam^-1 (CO), 8 mJy beam^-1 (HCN), 1.2 mJy beam^-1 (SO)

what.value: Mass-loss rate of R Dor (~1.6 10^-7 M_sun yr^-1)

evidence.quote: a mass-loss rate of $\sim$1.6 10$^{-7}$ M$_\odot$yr$^{-1}$ (cite: Ramstedt2014; Maercker2016)
it is close to the Sun, at a distance of only $\sim$59 pc (cite: Knapp2003)

what.value: Stellar disc radius at mm wavelength (~1.8 au / 0.03 arcsec)

evidence.quote: The stellar disc, known to have a radius of $\sim$1.8 au (0.03 arcsec) at mm wavelength (cite: Vlemmings2018), is here represented with a radius of 0.035 arcsec.

what.value: Temperature profile (~1100 K at 6 au, decreasing as r^-0.65)

evidence.quote: The high excitation energy of the SO$_2$ line prevents it from populating the outer CSE as the temperature can be expected to take a value of $\sim$1100 K at 6 au from the star and to decrease as $r^{-0.65}$ (cite: Decin2018; Homan2018; VandeSande2018).

what.value: 28SiO/H2 abundance of 5.5 10^-5 and relative abundances of CO, HCN

evidence.quote: We use a column density $N$ \[molecules cm$^{-3}$ arcsec\]=0.7 obtained by integration from $r$=0.8 to 1.0 arcsec for a $^{28}$SiO/H$_2$ abundance of 5.5 10$^{-5}$ (cite: VandeSande2018)
an isotopic ratio $^{29}$Si/$^{28}$Si=8% (cite: DeBeck2018)

what.value: SO2 and SO abundances relative to H2

evidence.quote: The abundance relative to H$_2$ is now of the form 5 10$^{-6}\exp[-(r/1.78)^2]$ (cite: Danilovich2016; Danilovich2020)

evidence.loc: Overall picture of the morpho-kinematics from a comparison between SO, 28SiO, CO and HCN line emissions
evidence.quote: Using abundances relative to H$_2$ given by (cite: VandeSande2018) and (cite: Danilovich2016) and an H$_2$ density corresponding to a mass-loss rate of $\sim$1.6 10$^{-7}$ M$_\odot$ year$^{-1}$ as was done in Section 3.2

evidence.loc: The blue stream: a possible companion?
evidence.quote: for a star mass $M$=1.4 M$_\odot$ (cite: Danilovich2017; DeBeck2018), $d$=$14.6\cos\theta_{\rm{bs}}/\sqrt{\sin\theta_{\rm{bs}}}$ au.

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image high-resolution 29SiO and SO2 data and re-image archival 28SiO, CO, and HCN data
recipe.method: Average visibilities over 20 s intervals, select 81 channels (69 km s^-1), calibrate with ALMA scripts, and deconvolve/clean with natural weighting and no continuum subtraction in both CASA and GILDAS (using GILDAS as default). Re-reduce 2013.1.00166.S lines in GILDAS without continuum subtraction.
key_parameters: time averaging = 20 s; 81 channels = 69 km s^-1 (0.854 km s^-1 bin); pixel size = 5x5 mas^2; natural weighting; no continuum subtraction
assumptions: Systemic velocity of R Dor is 7 km s^-1

recipe.goal: Extract and fit Doppler velocity spectra and azimuthal profiles in the inner layer (0.05 < R < 0.20 arcsec)
recipe.method: Divide inner CSE into concentric rings (0.05 arcsec wide) and quadrants; fit spectra with a continuum term plus Gaussian emission minus Gaussian outer-layer absorption at -4.0 km s^-1; fit azimuthal intensity and mean Doppler velocity distributions with sine waves A + B sin(omega - omega_0).
key_parameters: Rings: 50-100, 100-150, 150-200 mas; absorption center = -4.0 km s^-1, width sigma = 1.2 km s^-1; 3 sigma cut and |V_z| < 12 km s^-1 for sine fits
assumptions: Total absorption at V_z = -4.0 km s^-1 for 29SiO and zero outer absorption (A=0) for SO2

recipe.goal: Evaluate LTE radiative transfer and optical depth over the stellar disc
recipe.method: Calculate LTE unabsorbed emission epsilon and optical depth tau over 0.2 < r < 1.0 arcsec for 29SiO and SO2 and compare predicted self-absorbed emission against the observed 3-sigma upper limit over the stellar disc (R < 0.035 arcsec) at V_z ~ -4 km s^-1.
key_parameters: Stellar disc R < 0.035 arcsec; T = 270 K; Delta V = 2.8 km s^-1

recipe.goal: Measure kinematics and pointing of the south-eastern blue stream and test planetary companion hypothesis
recipe.method: Measure stream position in each frequency channel separately, fit straight lines to determine position angle, pointing offset from the star, and linear acceleration dV_z/dR; evaluate orbital travel distance of a putative companion during the gas transit time.
key_parameters: PA = 140 deg; PV slit width = +/- 3 au; R_1 ~ 10 au, R_2 ~ 30 au; |V_z1| ~ 7 km s^-1, |V_z2| ~ 18 km s^-1
assumptions: Circular orbit of companion around a 1.4 M_sun star; orbital axis aligned with gas rotation axis (PA = 10 +/- 5 deg)

recipe.goal: Model inner-layer 29SiO morpho-kinematics (rotation, expansion, turbulence, density, temperature)
recipe.method: Fit a 3D morpho-kinematic model of 29SiO emission across four concentric rings to constrain density n_0 and temperature T_0 at r = 0.1 arcsec (6 au), radial expansion, and Gaussian turbulent line broadening.
key_parameters: V_rot = 64 r (1 - 4r) km s^-1 for r <= 0.25 arcsec and 0 beyond; rotation axis PA = 10 deg, inclination = 20 deg
assumptions: T propto r^-0.65, n propto r^-2, Gaussian turbulent dispersion sigma_turb = V_turb exp(-0.5 (r - r_turb)^2 / Delta r_turb^2)

recipe.goal: Test whether extended 29SiO absorption is an interferometric short-spacing artefact
recipe.method: Simulate visibilities with CASA SIMOBSERVE for three isotropic sky brightness models (case 1: stellar continuum disc R < 0.04 arcsec; case 2: CSE disc R < 0.3 arcsec with absorbed stellar disc; case 3: sum of cases 1 and 2) using the actual antenna configuration, and compare baseline-dependent visibility amplitudes against real 29SiO visibilities at V_z = -4, +4 km s^-1, and continuum.
key_parameters: Case 1: 1 Jy/pixel for R < 0.04 arcsec; Case 2: 0.1 Jy/pixel for 0.04 < R < 0.3 arcsec; Case 3: Case 1 + Case 2

recipe.goal: Reconstruct 3D outflow geometry and model outer SiO self-absorption using SO, 28SiO, CO, and HCN
recipe.method: Deproject SO, 28SiO, CO, and HCN data cubes onto perpendicular outflow planes P1 (PA = 60 deg) and P2 (PA = 150 deg) using a radial velocity law V = V_term r / (r + r_1/2); compare observed radial flux profiles to optically thin LTE predictions; fit a radiative transfer model to 28SiO spectra in rings 0.35 < R < 0.55 arcsec and 0.65 < R < 0.85 arcsec.
key_parameters: V_term = 7 km s^-1, r_1/2 = 30 au (0.5 arcsec) for deprojection; rings 0.35-0.55 and 0.65-0.85 arcsec for 28SiO fit
assumptions: V = V_term r / (r + r_1/2); density propto r^-2; temperature T = T_0.5 r^-p; LTE radiative transfer

evidence.quote: It covers projected distances from the star reaching $\sim$30 au for the former (Figure \[figA1\]) and $\sim$20 au for the latter (Figure \[figA2\]) at a mean position angle of $\sim$140$^\circ$.

score_reason: All three ALMA project codes are public, spectral setups and imaging choices (natural weighting, 5 mas pixels, no continuum subtraction, channel widths) are clearly stated, and analytical equations and best-fit parameter tables are given in full; however, custom modelling scripts and exact cleaning thresholds are not released.
rediscovery_reason: Public archival ALMA data with well-defined geometric ring/quadrant spectral extractions, analytic Gaussian/sine fitting formulas, and explicit numeric tables (Tables 2, A1, A2) make the kinematic and absorption measurements straightforward to reproduce.
